selected_mathematical_checks: The ball Green lower bound follows from the Newton singularity at separation at most 2r and harmonic boundary correction at separation at least 3r on B_(4r). The two positive mass inequalities eliminate one mass with exponent pq-1. Holder then gives the stated L1 powers n-alpha0 and n-beta0. The estimates use p,q>1 and positive lower coefficients, not arbitrary sign sources.

The truncated Newtonian remainder is signed. Decomposing it as the actual nonnegative harmonic boundary extension minus the positive ball correction allows separate mean and gradient bounds. The resulting s^(-alpha0) and s^(-alpha0-1) errors in cross-energy, virial and endpoint averages have the displayed source-mass factors. Artificial boundary data are retained.

For Holder exponent theta, the original interval cutoff of length proportional to d gives a d^(theta-1) relative error. The new cutoff proportional to d^(1/theta), together with m>=max(n+3,1/theta+1), pays the coefficient endpoint variation. This is a new operation, not a repair of an originally claimed Holder pressure theorem. The high-level, low-level, far-localization and cap powers remain positive under the displayed k,N choices.

The positive reflected-kernel integral has factor 2 x_n y_n/S_n and integrand Q_t^(-n/2). Tangency plus the Lipschitz bound yields |S|<=2L and |D_X Q_t|<=2L Q_t, hence (n+2)L G. Joint dilation gives exactly (2-n)G. This avoids loss of cancellation, but is a fixed O(E) bound rather than an arbitrarily small relative error.

Testing the bounded nonnegative half-ball model with y_n(1-|y|^2/(4r^2))_+^3 removes both boundary terms: U and the test vanish on the plane, while the test and its first derivative vanish at the artificial sphere. The displayed Laplacian estimate and interior lower bound give a deliberately oversized explicit first-moment constant.

Odd reflection is applied only to the bounded harmonic extension, not to the nonlinear solution. The difference of ball correction kernels gains y_n, and its value additionally gains x_n. Integrating against the first source moment gives |h|<=B_n x_n/s and |grad h|<=B_n/s. Its normal derivative is not set to zero.

Dyadic annuli combine the reflected kernel decay |y|^(-n) with the first-moment growth r^(n-1) to give a geometric 1/R tail. The same estimate controls the nonzero plane normal derivative. These estimates apply to actual bounded PDE models, not arbitrary source measures.

The reflected interval calculation for e_n nonzero involves both s-t and s+t geometry because Re differs from e. The source parallel-line trapezoid operation therefore does not transfer unchanged. Selecting the reflected direction instead breaks the direct-kernel geometry. The stated obstruction concerns this method only, not Target L.

Discarding a thin plane layer under a known gradient envelope pays an additive fixed-scale error. Its normalization changes under the dilation in the pressure contradiction, so this does not prove the needed epsilon E+C_epsilon estimate. Both the full reflected pressure budget and the numerical full-ball pressure constant remain explicitly unpaid.

The source weighted interval comparison uses nonnegative extended integrals when a coefficient is zero, and the pressure proof pays two copies of the averaged layer loss. Parameter choices precede the large outer radius. Original qualitative compactness cannot supply an evaluable replacement by renaming its least constant.

Li-Souplet Lemma 4.4 uses zero positive part on both strip faces. Its displayed test bound has denominator (k-1)m-k; choosing m comparable to R uses bounded strip weight. The finite half-ball has additional top/lateral boundary terms and the later normal-convexity construction uses solution-dependent derivative bounds. This primary operation does not by itself furnish the report's missing numerical boundary threshold.
